The Great Performances and Emens’s arsenal of effects are a fun combination that emphasize Covenant’s connection to the horror genre — without tipping too far into the mega frightening or gory.
Covenant is beautifully written, beautifully acted, and beautifully told.
This is a confidently and expertly directed show in a genre that’s difficult to pull off even on screen, let alone a stage in a small theatre.

Ms. Stampley's nail-biting production is filled with powerful performances, edge-of-your-seat tension, hair-raising horror, terrifying special effects and a climax that will leave audiences breathless.
COVENANT is well-done! It's one of those exceptional plays that lends itself to an animated discussion post-show and serious contemplation on seeing it again.
Playwright York Walker’s writing is smooth and measured, peeling back the layers of an onion, careful not to give away too much too soon.
It's compelling blend of rumors, myth, truth, and gothic horror that keeps audiences on the edge of their seats, afraid to blink and missing the suspense.
“Covenant” is written with delicate nuance and lives deliciously onstage.
Walker is a generous and vivid writer who gifts each character with a soul-bearing monologue.
So, OK: first of all, I need to tell you that York Walker's Covenant , now playing at the Goodman Theatre, is an outstanding play.
The Chicago premiere of Covenant is a thrilling example of theatrical spectacle and storytelling at its finest.
It is bold! It is striking! It is powerful!

If you like shows where it feels like a puzzle and you’re slowly putting the pieces together thinking you know what it will be but are absolutely gobsmacked at the final picture, Covenant will be a good fit for you!

cn.t: Walker's Southern Gothic thriller earns strong praise for its atmospheric blend of faith, folklore, and supernatural dread, though some critics found themselves waiting for bigger scares to materialize.
